test_title: PYST 21: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 18 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a part of urban transport infrastructure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Irrigation canals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urban transport infrastructure** refers to systems and facilities designed to support the movement of people and goods within urban areas, ensuring efficient mobility and connectivity.
 
• **Metro systems**: These are rapid transit systems used in urban areas, such as subways or elevated railways, providing fast and efficient transport for city dwellers.
 
• **Highways**: These are major roadways that connect cities and towns, facilitating inter-urban and intra-urban travel. They are a crucial part of urban transport planning.
 
• **Rail networks**: These include trains and other railway systems that connect different parts of a city or region, aiding in the transport of passengers and goods.
 
• **Irrigation canals**, on the other hand, are part of agricultural infrastructure, designed to distribute water for farming purposes, and do not serve the purpose of urban transport. *Hence, irrigation canals are NOT a part of urban transport infrastructure.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metro Systems:**

 
 
• Metro systems are also known as subways, undergrounds, or rapid transit systems.
 
• Examples include the **Delhi Metro**, **London Underground**, and **New York Subway**.
 
• They are known for reducing traffic congestion and pollution in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Highways:**
 
 
• Highways are an essential component of urban and inter-urban connectivity.
 
• Examples in India include the **Golden Quadrilateral** and **North-South and East-West Corridors**.
 
• They are designed for high-speed vehicular traffic, often connecting major cities.
 
 
 
• **Rail Networks:**
 
 
• Urban rail networks include commuter trains and monorails.
 
• Examples: **Mumbai Suburban Railway**, **Kolkata Metro**.
 
• They are essential for reducing road traffic and promoting mass transportation in densely populated cities.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Canals:**
 
 
• Irrigation canals are used primarily in agriculture to supply water to fields.
 
• Examples include the **Indira Gandhi Canal** in Rajasthan and the **Upper Ganga Canal** in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• They do not contribute to urban transport systems but are vital for agricultural productivity.
